To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incidence of breast cancer is increasing in the elderly population, the majority of these patients are not treated with curative intent, and the prognosis is poor, even when they receive adjuvant treatment.

1) the risk of developing breast cancer increases with age; 2) the risk of dying from breast cancer decreases with age; 3) the risk of breast cancer mortality is higher in older patients with a high-risk breast tumor; and 4) breast cancer treatment is associated with increased mortality and morbidity in high-risk elderly women, but the benefit is still greater than the harm in this population.
